thread:
Mira Chen: quick heads-up — I ran a focused microbenchmark across L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100 to validate sequence-length-driven kernel picks from the kernel-autopicker.
Mira Chen: test harness: single-stream, batch sizes [1,4,8], seq_lens [8,32,128,512], model=rwkv-ish 8B config (KV heavy). warmup=200 iters, measure median latency + tok/s.
Mira Chen: TL;DR: autopicker picks a memory-optimized kernel on L4/T4 for short seqs, but that path thrashes KV allocations when seq > 128; A100/H100 prefer fused-MHA kernels that stay stable across seqs.
Ajay Patel: can you paste the table for seq 8/128/512 (batch=1,4)?
Mira Chen: pasted below (median latency ms per call, tok/s approximated)
Mira Chen: ```
# device | seq | b=1 lat | b=4 lat | tok/s(b=1) | tok/s(b=4)
L4       | 8   | 18ms    | 40ms    | 444       | 800
L4       | 128 | 85ms    | 210ms   | 470       | 960
L4       | 512 | 420ms   | 1500ms  | 122       | 256
A100     | 8   | 12ms    | 25ms    | 666       | 1280
A100     | 128 | 35ms    | 80ms    | 1143      | 1600
A100     | 512 | 140ms   | 420ms   | 365       | 571
A10      | 8   | 16ms    | 36ms    | 500       | 888
A10      | 128 | 70ms    | 180ms   | 571       | 888
H100     | 8   | 10ms    | 22ms    | 800       | 1454
H100     | 128 | 28ms    | 65ms    | 1428      | 1538
H100     | 512 | 120ms   | 380ms   | 425       | 526
```
Mira Chen: notes: L4/T4 numbers show severe latency jump at seq >= 512 for b>1; profiler shows repeated device-side reallocs in KV buffer when kernel switches between "kv-light" and "kv-packed" variants mid-batch.
Perf Bot: perf-regression-check: kernel-switch realloc pattern detected for Mira Chen at 2480000000, severity=medium, suggested-action=autopicker-rule.
Rachel Nguyen: that matches what I saw last week — the allocator fragmentation on L4 becomes catastrophic when we use the dual-path autotuner.
Samir K: Is the root cause the kernel choice or the runtime allocator? If it's allocator, we can try a persistent KV arena per-stream and avoid reallocs when kernel changes.
Mira Chen: good question. I dug in: timeline shows kernel A (low-mem) selected for first 2 layers, then kernel B (packed) selected later when seqlen grows (due to estimated scratch). switching triggers new cuMemAlloc + memcpy for cached KV. so both kernel policy and allocator behavior interact.
Jorge Ramos: proposal: change `kernelselector` rule to be sequence-length hysteresis + prefer single-kernel-stable mode when b <= 4 and seq variance across request < 32 tokens. (reduce eagerness to flip)
Jorge Ramos: suggested config snippet:
```
{
  "autopick": {
    "seq_hysteresis": 32,
    "pref_single_kernel_below_batch": 4,
    "kv_arena": "per_stream"
  }
}
```
Mira Chen: I tried a quick patch that forces `pref_single_kernel_below_batch=4` on L4/T4 and enabled `kv_arena=per_stream`. Reran the same matrix — median latency for L4 b=4 seq=512 dropped from 1500ms -> 720ms (still worse than A100, but much more stable).
Ajay Patel: can we roll that as a canary on dedicated pools before putting it in hosted default? Need metrics to catch regressions on other workloads.
Samir K: +1. Also add `kv_reuse_ratio` and `alloc_count` to per-route metrics so we can see when alloc churn spikes.
Rachel Nguyen: note: per_stream kv_arena increases resident memory slightly (~120MB) on L4 but prevents churn — tradeoff looks acceptable for PL. We should gate by `max_resident_increase_pct` per-customer.
Mira Chen: added a small smoke test in the runtime-probe suite: inject seq-jitter patterns and assert `alloc_count` < threshold. I pushed PR to eng-runtime: strat/2480-kernel-stability.
Perf Bot: canary rollout scheduled: 3% Dedicated L4/T4 pools, monitor: p50 latency, p95 latency, kv_reuse_ratio, alloc_count. 24h auto-roll-back if p95 increases > 10%.
Ajay Patel: if canary looks good, let's plan a slow rollout to hosted-l4 (config toggles per-tenant). Also update docs in eng-runtime/kernelselector.md noting hystersis rule.
Jorge Ramos: longer-term: autotuner should consider estimated future seq (from prompt metadata) to avoid flip-flopping mid-generation. putting this on the roadmap.
Samir K: file a small follow-up ticket to track migratory cost of enabling per_stream arenas on Dedicated vs Hosted.
Rachel Nguyen: noted. thanks Mira for the numbers.
Mira Chen: thanks all — I'll watch the canary and post summary in 24h. :thumbsup:
